claims.text: The controlled comparison uses equimolar CoCrFeNiTi, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each element, with composition held constant between the as-cast and annealed samples.
The as-cast CoCrFeNiTi starting alloy is a single-phase, chemically disordered solid solution.
The as-cast CoCrFeNiTi alloy has relatively low hardness and strength.
The as-cast CoCrFeNiTi alloy has good plasticity.
The as-cast CoCrFeNiTi alloy has good machinability.
The as-cast alloy has a relatively low level of intrinsic lattice distortion.
The as-cast alloy lacks nanoscale dislocation obstacles such as short-range order or precipitates.
Low lattice distortion and the absence of nanoscale obstacles permit relatively unhindered dislocation motion.
Relatively free dislocation motion causes the lower hardness and yield strength of the as-cast alloy.
Relatively free dislocation motion facilitates the plasticity of the as-cast alloy.
Annealing at approximately 600 °C for 1–2 hours will induce nanoscale ordered domains or fine secondary-phase precipitates without causing coarse phase separation.
Nanoscale ordered domains or fine precipitates impede dislocation glide through dislocation pinning.
Annealing-induced nanoscale ordering or precipitation will increase hardness and yield strength relative to the as-cast alloy.
The strengthening treatment will cause only a modest reduction in plastic strain rather than a complete loss of ductility.
Microscopy should find nanoscale ordered domains or finely dispersed precipitates in the annealed material that are absent from the as-cast material.
The proposed comparison uses room-temperature and 600 °C mechanical tests under quasi-static loading at approximately 10^-3 s^-1.
The hypothesis is limited to processing and testing temperatures up to approximately 600 °C.
Overly aggressive annealing can form coarse precipitates, while overly mild annealing can produce insufficient ordering, and either condition may prevent the expected strengthening.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant hardness and yield-strength increase, or failure to detect the proposed nanoscale structures, would falsify the mechanism.
